src: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy was completed in 112 patients, and conversion to open surgery was required in four because of dense adhesions in the Calot triangle.
Postoperative complications were graded according to the Clavien-Dindo classification; grade III or higher complications occurred in 6% of patients.
Anastomotic leak was the most common major complication after low anterior resection and required reoperation in two patients.
The mean operative time was 185 minutes and the mean intraoperative blood loss was 120 mL.
Surgical site infection developed in 5 patients and was managed with wound opening and dressing changes; one patient had a seroma.
All patients underwent a radical gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy, and an R0 resection was achieved in 95% of cases.
An ultrasound-guided transversus abdominis plane block was performed at the end of surgery to reduce postoperative opioid consumption.

src: Induction of anesthesia was performed with propofol and fentanyl, and the depth of anesthesia was monitored with the bispectral index.
Spinal anesthesia was used for most inguinal hernia repairs, whereas general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation was used for laparoscopic procedures.
Patients classified as ASA III had a higher rate of postoperative complications and a longer postoperative length of stay.

src: A temporary ileostomy was created to protect the colorectal anastomosis and was closed three months later.
Intraoperative frozen section confirmed negative margins, so no further resection was performed.
Robot-assisted surgery was associated with a shorter hospital stay but a longer operative time than open surgery.
A Lichtenstein repair with a polypropylene mesh was performed for the incarcerated inguinal hernia.
Palliative surgery was performed for an unresectable gastric cancer with gastric outlet obstruction.
Patients who received neoadjuvant therapy had a longer operative time.
